q01.key_idea: Count every circle once, the big ones and the small ones.
steps: The 2 blue ears are 2 circles. Each ear has a small white circle inside, so that is 2 more: 2 + 2 = 4.
The big yellow face is 1 circle: 4 + 1 = 5.
The 2 orange eyes are 2 circles: 5 + 2 = 7.
The purple mouth is 1 circle: 7 + 1 = 8.

choice_feedback.A: 5 only counts the ears, the white circles and the face. The eyes and the mouth are missing.
choice_feedback.C: 7 forgets one circle. Did you count the purple mouth or the white circles in the ears?
choice_feedback.E: 9 counts one circle too many. There are only 8.

q02.key_idea: From above you only see the top cube of each stack.
steps: From the front, the bottom row has 3 white cubes.
On the left, a dark grey cube sits on top. On the right, a light grey cube sits on top. The middle has nothing on top.
From above, the dark grey cube hides the white cube under it on the left. The light grey cube hides the white cube on the right.
In the middle we see the white cube. So from above: dark grey, white, light grey.

choice_feedback.A: All white is wrong. The dark grey and light grey cubes on top would be seen from above.
choice_feedback.C: The colours are in the wrong order. The left square must be dark grey and the middle one white.
choice_feedback.D: The colours are in the wrong order. The left square must be dark grey, not light grey.
choice_feedback.E: The middle and right squares are swapped. The light grey cube is on the right.

q03.key_idea: Add the 4 numbers in each bowl and compare the totals.
steps: 28 is the biggest total, and it is in bowl A.

q04.key_idea: Find each piece of the square in the kangaroo. The piece you cannot find is missing.
steps: The square has 7 pieces: 2 big triangles, 1 middle triangle, 2 small triangles, 1 square and 1 slanted piece with 4 sides.
The kangaroo has a small triangle for the ear and a small triangle for the arm.
It has 2 big triangles in the middle, the square turned on its corner, and the middle-sized triangle for the foot.
No part of the kangaroo is the slanted piece with 4 sides.

choice_feedback.B: This small triangle is in the kangaroo. It is the ear or the arm.
choice_feedback.C: The square is in the kangaroo, turned on its corner near the foot.
choice_feedback.D: This small triangle is in the kangaroo. It is the ear or the arm.
choice_feedback.E: This middle-sized triangle is in the kangaroo. It is the foot at the bottom.

q05.key_idea: Count the circles, triangles and squares on each boat and check both clues.
steps: Clue 1: more than 1 circle. Boat C has only 1 circle, so it is out.
Clue 2: 2 more triangles than squares. Count both on every other boat.
Boat A: 2 triangles, 1 square. Boat B: 3 triangles, 2 squares. Boat D: 1 triangle, 3 squares.
Boat E has 3 circles, 4 triangles and 2 squares. 2 + 2 = 4, so both clues fit.

choice_feedback.A: It has 2 triangles and 1 square. That is only 1 more triangle, not 2.
choice_feedback.B: It has 3 triangles and 2 squares. That is only 1 more triangle, not 2.
choice_feedback.C: It has only 1 circle, but Sara's boat has more than one.
choice_feedback.D: It has 1 triangle and 3 squares. It has fewer triangles than squares.

q06.key_idea: Compare the two bees and add up the cost of each missing piece.
steps: The bee on the right has only 1 eye. The second eye costs 1 point.
It has only 1 feeler on its head. The second feeler costs 3 points.
It has a wing on the left side only. The wing on the right costs 4 points.
It has no smile. The smile costs 5 points. 1 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 13.

choice_feedback.A: 9 is too few. 4 pieces are missing: an eye, a feeler, a wing and the smile.
choice_feedback.B: 10 forgets the second feeler, which costs 3 points.
choice_feedback.D: 12 forgets the eye, which costs 1 point.

q07.key_idea: When you unfold the paper, each hole gets a mirror twin on the other side of the fold.
steps: The fold is the dashed line on the right side of the folded paper.
The circle is at the top, far from the fold. The square is at the bottom, close to the fold.
When she unfolds, the circle gets a twin far from the fold on the other side. So both circles sit at the outer edges.
The square gets a twin close to the fold. So both squares sit next to the middle line.

choice_feedback.A: The holes are just copied, not mirrored. One circle ends up close to the fold.
choice_feedback.C: Here the twin of the circle is a square. A twin hole must have the same shape.
choice_feedback.D: All the holes are the same distance from the fold. But the circle was far from the fold and the square was close to it.
choice_feedback.E: This is the wrong way round. The circles are near the fold and the squares are far from it.

q08.key_idea: The cubes make no closed ring, so every cube after the first needs exactly 1 drop of glue.
steps: Look at how the 12 cubes touch. There is a row of 4 cubes at the front.
2 cubes stick out in front of that row. On the left, 2 cubes go back with 1 more on top. On the right, a tower of 3 cubes stands behind.
Nowhere do the cubes close into a ring. So start with 1 cube and add the others one at a time.
Each new cube touches just 1 cube already there, so it needs 1 drop. 12 - 1 = 11 drops.

choice_feedback.A: 8 drops are too few to hold 12 cubes together.
choice_feedback.B: 9 drops are too few. Every cube except the first needs its own drop.
choice_feedback.C: 10 drops would hold only 11 cubes. Hansi has 12 cubes.
choice_feedback.E: 12 drops would be 1 too many. The cubes make no ring, so only 12 - 1 = 11 drops are needed.

q09.key_idea: Take away the numbers you know, then share what is left between the two question marks.
steps: 18 - 12 = 6. So the two question marks together make 6.
Both question marks are the same number. 3 + 3 = 6.

q10.key_idea: First count the empty squares, then check that the pieces really fit.
steps: Count the white squares: 1 in the top row, 4 in the second row, 3 in the third row and 2 in the bottom row. 1 + 4 + 3 + 2 = 10.
Count the squares in each set: A has 4 + 3 + 3 = 10, B has 4 + 4 + 3 = 11, C has 3 + 4 + 3 = 10, D has 1 + 3 + 3 = 7, E has 4 + 4 + 1 = 9.
Only A and C have 10. Try A: the long straight piece goes down the left side, from the top.
The T piece fills the rest of the second row and pokes down into the third row. The small L piece fills the last 3 squares at the bottom left.

choice_feedback.B: These pieces have 11 squares, but there are only 10 white squares.
choice_feedback.C: It has 10 squares, but these pieces cannot fit together to fill the white space.
choice_feedback.D: These pieces have only 7 squares. 3 white squares would stay empty.
choice_feedback.E: These pieces have only 9 squares. 1 white square would stay empty.

q11.key_idea: Draw the line of dancers from first to last.
steps: Emma is in place 3.
3 dancers come after her: places 4, 5 and 6.
The last girl comes after them, in place 7.
So there are 7 dancers in all.

choice_feedback.A: With 4 dancers, nobody could stand between Emma and the last girl.
choice_feedback.B: With 5 dancers, only 1 girl would be between Emma and the last girl.
choice_feedback.C: With 6 dancers, only 2 girls would be between Emma and the last girl.
choice_feedback.E: With 8 dancers, 4 girls would be between Emma and the last girl.

q12.key_idea: Each of the 6 slices of the hexagon must look exactly like the triangle.
steps: Look at the triangle. Along its wide side is a small X. Under the X is a straight line across. Under that line is a pointed roof shape.
The hexagon is made of 6 triangles that meet in the middle, so each slice must show the X, the line and the roof.
In picture A every slice has a small X at the outside edge, a line across under it, and a roof shape under the line.
In the other pictures some part is missing or looks different.

choice_feedback.B: The X at the top and bottom is shut in a box with straight sides. The triangle has no box.
choice_feedback.C: There is no straight line across under the X, and several lines stop with gaps instead of joining up.
choice_feedback.D: There is no roof shape under the line. Instead there is a second line across.
choice_feedback.E: The X is much bigger and wider than the X on the triangle.

review.note: Key A matches the blind solver (medium confidence). The options differ only in small details in low-resolution raster images; please check the described details (B boxed X, C no line under X and broken lines, D second line instead of roof, E wide X) against the pictures.

q13.key_idea: Use the clues one at a time, starting with the youngest.
steps: The cakes show 8, 7, 6, 5 and 4. Vittorio is the youngest, so he gets 4.
Ali is 1 year older than Lea, and Lea is 2 years older than Josef. So Ali is 3 years older than Josef.
From 5, 6, 7 and 8, the only numbers 3 apart are 5 and 8. So Josef is 5 and Ali is 8.
Lea is 5 + 2 = 7. The cake left over is 6, and that is Sophie's.

choice_feedback.A: 8 is Ali's cake. Ali is 3 years older than Josef.
choice_feedback.B: 7 is Lea's cake. Lea is 2 years older than Josef.
choice_feedback.E: 4 is Vittorio's cake, because he is the youngest.

q14.key_idea: Find how many apples were taken in all, then share that number equally between the 3 bags.
steps: After Maria takes some, the bags have 3 + 4 + 6 = 13 apples.
At the start there were 19 apples. 19 - 13 = 6 apples were taken.
She took the same number from each of the 3 bags. 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
Check: the bags had 5, 6 and 8 apples. 5 + 6 + 8 = 19.

choice_feedback.A: Taking 1 from each bag takes only 3 apples, but 6 were taken.
choice_feedback.C: Taking 3 from each bag takes 9 apples, but only 6 were taken.
choice_feedback.D: Taking 4 from each bag takes 12 apples, but only 6 were taken.
choice_feedback.E: Taking 5 from each bag takes 15 apples, but only 6 were taken.

q15.key_idea: On every night one frog sings and the other two listen.
steps: There were 9 nights, so 9 songs.
The second frog listened to 5 songs, so it sang on the other nights: 9 - 5 = 4 songs.
The first frog sang 2 songs. The third frog sang the rest: 9 - 2 - 4 = 3 songs.
The third frog listened when it did not sing: 9 - 3 = 6 songs.

choice_feedback.A: 7 would mean the third frog sang only 2 songs. It sang 3.
choice_feedback.C: 5 is how many songs the second frog listened to, not the third frog.
choice_feedback.D: 4 is how many songs the second frog sang.
choice_feedback.E: 3 is how many songs the third frog sang, not how many it listened to.
